# Mary Stubbs

[Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow)

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P38](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0038)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mary-creature  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS WINIFRED INTERVENES P4](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

Mary Stubbs has a full face with rosy cheeks and meticulously crimped hair, topped by a fresh blue velvet cap featuring a scarlet rosette. Her peculiar, unusual eyes are pale, white, and glowing, though heavy weeping has at times left them resembling singed openings in a blanket. She is also noted for having long, pliable fingers.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P31](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P11](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0011), [v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XXXI. RUPERT DOES PENANCE P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028)_

## Personality

Mary Stubbs is a remarkably clever yet unwise young girl. She possesses an exceptional work ethic, devouring labor like no one else, and is known for being savagely blunt while remaining unbothered by others due to not being excessively thin-skinned. Among her many talents, she has a good ear for music, excels at playing the jew's-harp, and is a skilled cook and bread dough maker. Additionally, she can project extraordinary shadow art on walls with her long, pliable fingers and tells spine-tingling ghost stories, despite maintaining that specters actually frighten her.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P19](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0019), [v5 CHAPTER VI. ## History

Mary Stubbs grew up without being raised in a traditional home, spending two years at an asylum and attending school for four winters after being taken in by Mrs. [Grimble](../character/grimble.md). Her grandfather had been a wealthy man, but her parents squandered the fortune. After escaping her abusive guardian, Mary hid in an old barn where she was discovered by the Ashdown children. She shared her tragic past and fears of beatings and damnation with them, and she was arranged to sleep in the parsonage garret room. Refusing to attend school, Mary spent her days cleaning the manse, sparring with [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md), and entertaining local children with ghost stories and unique tricks, though she also terrorized [Tessa Carrow](../character/tessa-carrow.md) with a dried codfish in the street.

Upon learning that Mrs. [Grimble](../character/grimble.md) had died, Mary faced the threat of being sent back to the asylum. However, Miss Winifred agreed to adopt her, and the local children presented Mary with farewell gifts. Adopting a fine new wardrobe, Mary frequently brought local gossip to the Ashdown children, informing them of financial threats against their father's parish, village scandal after they cleaned carpets on a Sunday, and rumors surrounding their father's potential remarriage to [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md). She also continued to gather with the children, startling them with ghost stories at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) and sharing town gossip regarding Rupert's antics and Clementine's refusal of Mr. Ashdown's proposal.

## Quotes

> "Of course. A better deed fits a better day. Just provide me with a thread and needle, and turn your eyes away in case you get squeamish."
>
> — Mary Stubbs — [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P7](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0007)

> "For four winters after I arrived at Mrs. Grimble’s, I attended school, and I have no desire for more. Being constantly scolded because my homework was incomplete has made me thoroughly fed up. There was no time for me to complete homework."
>
> — Mary Stubbs — [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P12](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0012)

> "Cats are completely useless to me anyway. Their origin is the devil. Look at their eyes and you’ll know it’s true. Oh well, I guess if old Martha refuses, she refuses. Still, seeing fine food wasted makes me furious."
>
> — Mary Stubbs — [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P18](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0018)

> "Had my family merely spanked me, I would have considered it affection. Ah well, the world lacks fairness. Taking my fair portion of beatings wouldn’t bother me, yet I have received far too many."
>
> — Mary Stubbs — [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P38](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0038)

> "If you were aware of a few of the expressions I might utter if I chose, you would not create this much of a commotion about darn. Furthermore, you are well aware that I have not uttered a single lie since my arrival here."
>
> — Mary Stubbs — [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P40](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0040)

## Relationships

### [Grace](../character/grace.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/grace--mary-stubbs.md)

Mary becomes a frequent walking companion and friend to [Grace](../character/grace.md) after being discovered hiding in a barn as a runaway. [Grace](../character/grace.md) helps arrange shelter for Mary, and Mary later spends time playing with [Grace](../character/grace.md) and the other local children while sharing stories and tricks. [Grace](../character/grace.md) also receives warning from Mary about household calendar errors and parish gossip that could affect her family.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), +12 more_

### [Ida Ashdown](../character/ida-ashdown.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ida-ashdown--mary-stubbs.md)

[Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) acts as a close playmate and mentor to Mary, even helping teach her basic domestic tasks like washing plates. After Mary shares her fears of beatings and damnation, [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) comforts her in the parsonage garret, reassures her when her past threatens to catch up with her, and intervenes to help secure her adoption. Though they share a close bond, Mary occasionally frightens [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) with heavy discussions on faith and rumors of her father remarrying.

### [Kit Carrow](../character/kit-carrow.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/kit-carrow--mary-stubbs.md)

Kit is a favored companion of Mary among the local children who gather at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Despite playing together and sharing stories, tension arises when Mary scolds the manse children in the graveyard over rumors and gossip caused by their wild behavior. Prompted by Mary's reprimand, Kit suggests establishing a [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) so the children can manage their behavior.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P9](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0009), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P15](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0015), +13 more_

### [Winifred Tolley](../character/winifred-tolley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary-stubbs--winifred-tolley.md)

Miss Winifred serves as an authority figure who manages and interrogates Mary regarding her wild behavior and upbringing. After learning of Mary's situation, [Winifred](../character/winifred-tolley.md) steps in to adopt her alongside her husband to prevent Mary from being sent to an asylum. Mary performs household duties such as knitting under Winifred's supervision, though she often runs off afterward to pass along overheard adult conversations and gossip to the local children.
